verses.1:1: The burden of Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.1:2: The Lord is a jealous God, avenging with wrath; the Lord takes vengeance on His adversaries, and He Himself removes His enemies.
verses.1:3: The Lord is longsuffering, and great is His strength, and the Lord will by no means acquit; His way is in complete destruction and in violent shaking, and the clouds are the dust of His feet.
verses.1:4: He threatens the sea and dries it up, and makes all the rivers desolate. Bashan and Carmel are diminished, and the blossoms of Lebanon have failed.
verses.1:5: The mountains quaked because of Him, and the hills were shaken; and the earth shrank back from His presence—the whole world and all who dwell in it.
verses.1:6: Who shall endure before the face of His anger? And who shall withstand in the wrath of His fury? His fury melts dominions, and the rocks were shattered because of Him.
verses.1:7: The Lord is good to those who wait upon Him in the day of affliction, and He knows those who revere Him.
verses.1:8: And with a flood on its course He will make a complete end; darkness shall pursue those who rise up and His enemies.
verses.1:9: What do you devise against the Lord? He Himself will make a complete end; He will not take vengeance twice for the same thing in affliction;
verses.1:10: for even to its foundation it shall be laid waste, and like entangled bindweed it shall be devoured, and like stubble full of dryness.
verses.1:11: Out of you shall come forth a scheme against the Lord, counseling wicked things in opposition.
verses.1:12: Thus says the Lord who rules over many waters: "Even so they shall be separated, and your report shall not be heard anymore.
verses.1:13: And now I will break his rod from you, and I will tear the bonds apart."
verses.1:14: And the Lord shall command concerning you: "Nothing of your name shall be sown anymore; out of the house of your god I will destroy the carved images, and cast images I will make your grave." For swift—
verses.2:1: Behold, upon the mountains are the feet of him who brings good tidings and proclaims peace! Keep your feasts, O Judah, pay your vows, for they shall no more continue to pass through you to decay.
verses.2:2: It is finished; it has been taken away. He has gone up breathing into your face, delivering from affliction. Watch the way, brace your loins, be exceedingly valiant in strength;
verses.2:3: for the Lord has turned back the arrogance of Jacob as the arrogance of Israel, because those who shake out have shaken them out, and their vine branches; they have destroyed
verses.2:4: the weapons of their might from among men, mighty men mocking in fire; the reins of their chariots are in the day of his preparation, and the horsemen shall be thrown into confusion
verses.2:5: in the ways, and the chariots shall be thrown into disorder and entangled together in the broad squares; their appearance is like torches of fire and like lightning darting through.
verses.2:6: And their nobles shall remember, and they shall flee by day and grow weak in their march, and they shall hasten to her walls and prepare their outposts.
verses.2:7: The gates of the cities have been opened wide, and the palaces have collapsed,
verses.2:8: and the foundation was uncovered, and she herself was going up, and her maidservants were led away like doves moaning in their hearts.
verses.2:9: And Nineveh—her waters are like a pool of water; and they, fleeing, did not stand, and there was none who looked back.
verses.2:10: They plundered the silver, they were plundering the gold, and there was no end to her adornment; they have been weighed down with all her desirable vessels.
verses.2:11: Shaking out and tossing up and boiling over, and shattering of the heart, and loosening of knees and pangs upon all loins, and the face of all is like the scorching of a pot.
verses.2:12: Where is the dwelling place of the lions, and the pasture that was for the cubs? Where did a lion go, that a lion's cub might enter there, and there was none to terrify?
verses.2:13: A lion seized enough for his cubs and strangled for his lions, and filled his lair with prey and his dwelling place with plunder.
verses.2:14: "Behold, I am against you," says the Lord Almighty, "and I will burn up your multitude in smoke, and the sword shall devour your lions; and I will destroy your prey from the earth, and your deeds shall no longer be heard."
verses.3:1: O city of blood, wholly false, full of unrighteousness—prey shall not be handled.
verses.3:2: The sound of whips and the sound of the rumbling of wheels, and of a pursuing horse and of a bounding chariot,
verses.3:3: and of a mounting horseman and of a gleaming sword and flashing weapons, and of a multitude of wounded and a heavy downfall; and there was no end to her nations, and they shall grow weak in their bodies because of the multitude of harlotry.
verses.3:4: A fair and charming harlot, a mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her harlotry and peoples by her sorceries.
verses.3:5: "Behold, I am against you," says the Lord God Almighty, "and I will uncover your hinder parts over your face, and I will show nations your shame and kingdoms your dishonor;
verses.3:6: and I will cast abomination upon you according to your uncleannesses, and I will make you an example;
verses.3:7: and it shall come to pass that everyone who sees you shall go down from you and say, 'Wretched Nineveh! Who shall groan for her? From where shall I seek comfort for her?'"
verses.3:8: Prepare a portion, tune the string, prepare a portion, O Ammon, who dwells among the rivers; water is all around her, whose dominion is the sea, and water is her walls.
verses.3:9: And Ethiopia is her strength, and Egypt, and there is no limit to the flight, and the Libyans became her helpers.
verses.3:10: Yet she herself shall go into exile as a captive, and they shall dash her infants to the ground at the head of all her streets; and for all her glorious things they shall cast lots, and all her nobles shall be bound with manacles.
verses.3:11: And you shall become drunk and shall be overlooked, and you shall seek for yourself a standing place from enemies.
verses.3:12: All your strongholds are fig trees having watchmen; if they are shaken, they shall fall into the mouth of the eater.
verses.3:13: Behold, your people are like women in your midst; the gates of your land shall surely be opened wide to your enemies, and fire shall devour your bars.
verses.3:14: Draw for yourself water for the siege, and strengthen your strongholds; step into the clay and be trampled in chaff; grow stronger than brick.
verses.3:15: There fire shall devour you, the sword shall destroy you, it shall devour you like a locust, and you shall be weighed down like a crawling locust.
verses.3:16: You have multiplied your merchandise more than the stars of heaven; the crawling locust rushed forth and flew away.
verses.3:17: Your mixed multitude leaped out like a wingless locust, like a locust mounted upon a hedge in a day of frost; the sun rose, and it leaped away, and did not know its place. Woe to them!
verses.3:18: Your shepherds have slumbered, O Assyrian king; he has put your rulers to sleep; your people have departed to the mountains, and there was none to receive them.
verses.3:19: There is no healing for your shattering; your wound is inflamed; all who hear the report of you shall clap their hands over you, for upon whom has your wickedness not come continually?

notes.1:3: Greek "athoon ouk athooei" (literally, "He will not acquit an innocent one") is an emphatic Septuagint idiom rendering a Hebrew infinitive absolute, meaning the Lord will certainly not acquit anyone as guiltless.
notes.1:6: Greek "tekei archas" ("melts dominions") reflects the Septuagint text, differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "is poured out like fire."
notes.1:7: Greek "tois hypomenousin auton" ("to those who wait upon Him") is a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a stronghold."
notes.1:14: The Septuagint ends 1:14 with "hoti tacheis" ("For swift—"), connecting it directly to "the feet" at the opening of 2:1, whereas the Masoretic Text concludes 1:14 with "for you are vile."
notes.2:1: Greek "eis palaiosin" ("to decay") renders the Hebrew word often translated "wickedness" or "Belial" as wearing out or growing old.
notes.2:2: Greek "emphyson" ("breathing") and "exairoumenos" ("delivering") reflect the Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "scatterer" and "guard."
notes.2:7: Greek "poleon" ("cities") is the Septuagint reading, differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "rivers."
notes.2:11: Greek "proskauma chytras" ("the scorching of a pot") reflects the Septuagint understanding of the rare Hebrew phrase rendered "grow pale" in the Masoretic Text.
notes.3:1: Greek "ou pselaphethesetai thera" ("prey shall not be handled") reflects a Septuagint reading of the Hebrew verb ("does not depart") as "to touch or feel."
notes.3:3: Greek "ethnesin" ("nations") appears in the Septuagint where the Masoretic Text reads "corpses," and the Septuagint attaches "because of the multitude of harlotry" to the close of 3:3 rather than 3:4.
notes.3:8: Greek "Prepare a portion, tune the string, prepare a portion, O Ammon" is a distinctive Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew text ("Are you better than No-Amon [Thebes]?"), retaining the Greek form "Ammon."
notes.3:12: Greek "skopous" ("watchmen") is the Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "first-ripe figs."
notes.3:17: Greek "ouai autois" ("Woe to them!") reflects the Septuagint reading of the Hebrew consonants ("Where are they?") as an exclamation of woe.
